subject: Exhibit B - Fee transition and stability corridor (redline)
messages:
From: Heather Olson <heather@olson.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Olson Legal <contracts@olson.ai>, Marcus Reed <marcus.reed@novushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Exhibit B redline - request for stability protections

Karthik,

Thanks for circulating Exhibit B. Our legal team reviewed and we have one material concern: the pricing schedule as written allows for unilateral per-unit fee adjustments tied to model upgrades that could materially increase our monthly run-rate during the first 12 months post-commencement.

Specifically, we need a stability corridor (floor/cap) around the per-token fee that both limits downside and provides predictability during the model transition period. We propose the language in the attached redline: a 6-month staged increase with an absolute cap of +15% on per-token rates from the executed exhibit rate, and a mutual rollback if downstream unit economics materially change.

High level asks:
- Insert a “Stability Corridor” mechanism in Exhibit B that limits increases to +15% and sets a 5% floor during the first 12 months.
- Add a defined “Material Regression” clause to allow Novus to request rollback and trigger a joint evaluation.
- Require 30 days’ notice for any fee variant tied to model or quantization changes.

We attached our proposed redline (Novus_ExhibitB_redline.docx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept corridor language or propose alternative guardrails?

Heather Olson
Senior Counsel, Olson Legal
heather@olson.ai

Attachment: Novus_ExhibitB_redline.docx (tracked changes)

Heather — would Novus accept staged increases instead of a single immediate cap? If not, flag preferred alternative.

Thanks Karthik — looping in redline suggestions below. I read Novus' doc and agree a corridor is the right commercial compromise; we should tighten definitions so it’s implementable operationally.

Key legal edits (summary):
- Define “Baseline Unit Rate” as the per-token fee in the executed Exhibit B and use that anchor for all percentage calculations.
- Replace Novus’ open rollback language with a trigger-based “Material Regression” definition: (i) >= 20% increase in per-session latency or (ii) >= 10% drop in task-level success metrics measured on Novus' provided eval set over a 14-day window post-rollout. This gives both sides objective measures.
- Staged corridor language: 0–90 days: Baseline Unit Rate (no increase); 91–180 days: up to +8% on Baseline; 181–365 days: up to +15% on Baseline.
- Notice: 30 days' written notice required for planned fee changes; emergency security or compliance-driven overrides allowed with 14 days' notice and written justification.

Below is a clean clause you can forward to Novus. Ben — please sanity check the percentages and confirm the impact sheet (example in separate attachment):

--- Proposed Exhibit B clause (clean) ---
Stability Corridor: 
For a period of twelve (12) months following the Effective Date, the per-unit fee set forth in Exhibit B (the “Baseline Unit Rate”) shall be subject to a staged stability corridor as follows: (a) Days 0–90: Baseline Unit Rate; (b) Days 91–180: up to eight percent (8%) increase above the Baseline Unit Rate; (c) Days 181–365: up to fifteen percent (15%) increase above the Baseline Unit Rate. Any proposed increase under this section shall be delivered to Customer in writing at least thirty (30) days prior to the effective date.

Material Regression: 
Customer may request a joint evaluation if, following the introduction of a model or serving change, Customer observes (i) a twenty percent (20%) or greater increase in average per-session latency for a representative workload, or (ii) a ten percent (10%) or greater decrease in model task success as measured against Customer-supplied evaluation prompts, in each case over a rolling fourteen (14) day window; provided, however, that Customer shall provide Redwood written notice with supporting metrics and logs. If the parties confirm Material Regression, Redwood shall use commercially reasonable efforts to remediate or roll back the change; if remediation is not feasible, the parties shall negotiate a reasonable rollback of fees pro rata for the affected period.

--- end clause ---

If everyone is OK with the objective trigger thresholds and the 30-day notice, I’ll put this in a tracked version and send back.

Laura Bennett

Karthik / Laura — ran financial sensitivity on the proposed corridor. Short summary: staged increases smooth impact and are acceptable from a revenue recognition and procurement stance. Attached is a simplified impact table (pricing-impact-estimate.xlsx).

Numbers (illustrative):
- Baseline annualized run-rate at current consumption: $2.4M
- If +8% applies months 4–6, incremental ARR ~ +$16k/month during that band (one-off uplift scaling with consumption).
- If +15% applies months 7–12, incremental ARR ~ +$40k/month in that band.
- We recommend the +8% / +15% bands but ask for two operational clarifications: (1) retroactive true-up treatment for usage measured in final billing period of a month; (2) whether caches/prefix crediting will be excluded from corridor calculations (we prefer excluding cached tokens to avoid double-counting).

I confirm we can live with the trigger thresholds Laura proposed, subject to the caching carve-out and a simple true-up line in Exhibit B: 
"Any increased fees under the Stability Corridor shall be applied to billable tokens excluding those credited by Redwood caching mechanisms; final monthly invoices may include a true-up to account for usage reconciliations."

Attachment: pricing-impact-estimate.xlsx

Karthik / Laura / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear proposed language. Novus is generally comfortable with a staged approach but we have three follow-ups: 

1) Floor: we still need a minimum guarantee so our pricing exposure downward is limited if Redwood introduces a materially lower unit in some circumstances. Can we formalize a 5% floor (i.e., the per-token fee shall not fall below 95% of the Baseline Unit Rate during the first 12 months without mutual written consent)?

2) Caching carve-out: Novus accepts the carve-out as written by Ben provided we get a short audit right (quarterly sampling) to verify token classification (cache vs billable).

3) Rollback mechanics: the Material Regression definition is acceptable, but Novus requests (a) an automatic 15-day remediation window following notice, and (b) failure to remediate entitles Novus to a pro rata fee rollback for the period impacted, capped at the aggregate increased amount.

If you can incorporate the floor language, the 15-day remediation cadence and the sampling audit right into your tracked version, we can move to a sign-off call next week and wrap Exhibit B.

Heather Olson
